cards.explanation: The answer is that He gathers the nations down into one valley. The LORD says, “I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat.” (Joel 3:2) He says it for the time when He restores Judah and Jerusalem. All the nations are included, friends.

The answer is how they treated His people Israel. The LORD says, “There I will enter into judgment against them concerning My people, My inheritance, Israel…” (Joel 3:2) The judgment is about what was done to His people. That's the whole case, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says Israel was scattered “…as they divided up My land.” (Joel 3:2) He calls it His. He calls the people His too, His inheritance. So the nations weren't just splitting up some empty ground.

The answer is False. The LORD says that if they retaliate, “…I will swiftly and speedily return your recompense upon your heads.” (Joel 3:4) No slow rolling and no waiting around. When He says swiftly, He means swiftly.

The answer is the Greeks. The LORD says, “You sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks, to send them far from their homeland.” (Joel 3:6) The point was to send them far away. I think that's a hard thing to read, friends.

The answer is that they'll be sold to the people of Judah. The LORD says, “I will sell your sons and daughters into the hands of the people of Judah…” (Joel 3:8) Then the people of Judah will sell them to the Sabeans, a distant nation. The same thing they did to Judah comes back around to them, which is what He meant by returning it on their heads.
The answer is the Sabeans. The LORD says the people of Judah “…will sell them to the Sabeans…” and calls them a distant nation. (Joel 3:8) The far-off buyer is the one named in the text, friends.

The answer is that they turn their farm tools into weapons. The call is, “Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning hooks into spears.” (Joel 3:10) Tools made for farming get turned into tools for war. If somebody did that to my cookie stamper, I'd need a long sit-down.

The answer is sit down. The LORD says, “…for there I will sit down to judge all the nations on every side.” (Joel 3:12) The nations are told to be roused and advance to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. He is the one who sits down to judge them, friends.

The answer is because their wickedness is great. The text says, “the wine vats overflow because their wickedness is great.” (Joel 3:13) The picture is a winepress packed to the brim. It's a serious verse, friends, so I'll let it stand.

The answer is near. The text says, “For the Day of the LORD is near in the valley of decision.” (Joel 3:14) Not far off, not already past. Just before that, the verse says, “Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision!”

The answer is True. The text says, “The sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will no longer shine.” (Joel 3:15) Even the lights in the sky go dim. That comes right after the verse that says the Day of the LORD is near. So you can stand on True for this one, friends.

The answer is a refuge and a stronghold. The text says, “But the LORD will be a refuge for His people, a stronghold for the people of Israel.” (Joel 3:16) The verse says the LORD will roar from Zion and raise His voice from Jerusalem, and heaven and earth will tremble. Even then, He is a refuge and a stronghold for His people. That's a comfort, friends.

The answer is False. The text says, “Jerusalem will be holy, never again to be overrun by foreigners.” (Joel 3:17) The words are “never again,” so foreigners will not overrun it. That's the promise, friends.

The answer is the house of the LORD. The text says, “…a spring will flow from the house of the LORD to water the Valley of Acacias.” (Joel 3:18) The spring flows from His house to water that valley. The verse also says all the streams of Judah will run with water.

The answer is because of their violence against Judah. Egypt and Edom will be desolate “…because of the violence done to the people of Judah, in whose land they shed innocent blood.” (Joel 3:19) That's the reason the text gives. It's a heavy verse, friends, and I won't make light of it.

The answer is forever. The text says, “But Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.” (Joel 3:20) Egypt and Edom end up desolate, but Judah stays lived in. A long, long time, friends.
